maintainer_comments.body:
The problem of a slow INFO command is not the latency of INFO itself, but it can cause other commands to be slow when they wait for the server to run the slow INFO command.

Moving the `getrusage()` calls to cron (run with period 100ms) will make the INFO command faster, but instead we run getrusage every 100ms in the background. This can cause latency spikes to other commands during the time when this cron task is running.

Maybe a better solution is to do a lazy update of all this memory stats

maintainer_comments.author: zuiderkwast
maintainer_comments.body:
The `maxmemory` tests are failing:

```
*** [err]: maxmemory - is the memory limit honoured? (policy allkeys-random) in tests/unit/maxmemory.tcl
Expected [s used_memory] < (1120264+4096) (context: type eval line 26 cmd {assert {[s used_memory] < ($limit+4096)}} proc ::test)
```

`s used_memory` calls INFO and extracts the `used_memory` field. It adds 4096 bytes to account for the memory usage of INFO itself, but I believe it uses more than that.

`sdsMakeRoomFor(info, 4096);` results in an alloc

maintainer_comments.author: zuiderkwast
maintainer_comments.body:
I think: If this test passed before, it means the INFO command didn't use so much memory. 4096 is probably enough for the full INFO reply, no?

A simple solution is to use `sdsMakeRoomFor(info, 2048);` instead. It will result in 4096 bytes capacity. Isn't it enough?
